newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland, April 30.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Wednesday.
- Ireland's economic boom could continue for at least another decade if prudent policies are followed at home, according to the country's leading economic forecast centre.
- On a day when a bright future was outlined for the economy, the Irish currency faced the short-term danger of a nosedive against sterling.
- A system of funding politics with taxpayers money will be pushed through the Irish parliament before the general election, which must take place in 1997.

- Ireland's hosting of the 9.2 million Irish pounds World Equestrian Games in 1998 was in serious doubt on Tuesday after Nissan Ireland, the Game's title sponsor, pulled the plug on any further sponsorship investment beyond 450,000 punts.
- Unemployment will fall dramatically over the coming years while the economy will continue to grow by more than five per cent a year, according to a new report published today.

- In a pre-election move, Irish cabinet ministers have approved major new tax incentives for businesses investing around the state's seven regional airports and in two unemployment blackspots in Dublin.

- Loyalist prisoners remained in control of two sections in a Northern Ireland prison on Tuesday after a day of protests. - Amid intense security to ensure bomb threats do not disrupt next Saturday's Eurovision Song Contest in Dublin, Ireland is now favourite to win.
- A multi-million pound tax break for Ireland's regional airports has been given the green light by the Irish government to attract hi-tech industries and thousands of jobs.
- Priests in County Galway have refused to use local water for baptising children because the water is teeming with worms.
